device.description: Quad 16-bit voltage-output DAC with 2.5-V internal reference, 24-bit SPI write-only interface, ENABLE, LDAC, RST with zero/mid-scale select (RSTSEL)
device.note: dac8565.pdf (SBAS411C) p.4 power requirements (AVDD 2.7-5.5 V, IOVDD 1.8-5.5 V) and logic levels vs IOVDD, p.5 pin configuration and descriptions, p.6-7 serial write operation and timing, p.25 data format (Table 1), p.26 enable/disable internal reference (Tables 2-4), p.27 serial interface, asynchronous reset, input shift register (Table 5), p.28 control matrix (Table 6), p.29 SYNC interrupt, power-on reset, LDAC and ENABLE pin, p.30 power-down modes (Table 7)

registers.name: PWR
registers.note: internal: per channel PD0 (PDx_EN, DB16) and PD1:PD2 (PDx, DB15:DB14) of the last power-down word written to that channel's buffer; a data word to the channel clears PDx_EN (power-down table: 1 01 1 kohm, 1 10 100 kohm, 1 11 / 1 00 Hi-Z)

registers.name: REFCTL
registers.note: internal reference mode (DB13, DB12 of the reference words): 00 automatic/default (010000h), 10 always powered down (012000h), 01 always powered up (011000h)

commands.name: BROADCAST UPDATE ALL FROM BUFFERS
commands.note: LD1 LD0 = 11, DB18 = 0: all channels load from their buffers; every device responds regardless of address

commands.name: BROADCAST WRITE ALL AND LOAD
commands.note: LD1 LD0 = 11, DB18 = 1, PD0 = 0: SR data to every channel's buffer and DAC register

commands.name: BROADCAST POWER-DOWN ALL
commands.note: LD1 LD0 = 11, DB18 = 1, PD0 = 1: power-down condition PD1:PD2 to every channel

commands.name: INTERNAL REFERENCE MODE
commands.note: reference words 010000h (default/automatic), 011000h (always on), 012000h (always off); shown with address bits 00, accepted at the device's own address

protocol.note: 24-bit word: DB23-DB22 0 0, LD1 LD0 (DB21-DB20), DB19 0, DAC select (DB18-DB17), PD0 (DB16), DB15-DB0 data (or PD1 PD2 in DB15-DB14 when PD0 = 1). Decoded at the 24th SCLK falling edge; SYNC rising earlier discards the word

pages: p.4 (supplies, logic inputs), p.5 (pins), p.6-7 (timing), p.25 (data format, Table 1), p.26 (reference words, Tables 2-4), p.27-28 (serial interface, RST, Tables 5-6), p.29 (SYNC interrupt, power-on reset, LDAC, ENABLE), p.30 (power-down, Table 7)
notModeled: analog outputs and output buffers (VOUTx never driven); power-down output loads stored in PWR only

the power-down condition is data in the buffer (TR/DR bits 17-16) and takes effect when the buffer is loaded; the model stores it per channel in PWR at once and clears it on the next data word to that channel. Loads of a power-down word (LD = 01, broadcast) do not change the DAC data register; LD = 10 loads all DAC registers from the buffers
ENABLE high: the device ignores the serial port; modeled by gating every command on the ENABLE level (STRAP.EN)
LDAC is a rising-edge trigger; synchronous updates use the LD1:LD0 load commands (LDAC tied low)
no read-back: the interface is write-only
IOVDD 1.8-2.7 V is allowed with degraded timing; vcc uses the 1.8-5.5 V IOVDD range of the power requirements table
SCLK limits (50 / 25 MHz) and setup/hold times
internal 2.5-V reference (REFCTL stored only; VREFH/VREFOUT never driven); the reference words are decoded with LD1:LD0 = 00, DAC select 00 and DB15:DB14 = 00 as in Tables 2-4

RSTSEL selects zero-scale reset with straight binary (USB) coding (low) or mid-scale reset with two's complement (BTC) coding (high); the stored code after reset is 0 in both cases (Table 1), so the register reset is 0 and the coding is analog-only
DB23/DB22 must be 0 except in broadcast words
variants: dac8565.pdf covers only the DAC8565 (A-D grades differ in accuracy/reference drift). DAC8564 is the same core with A0/A1 address pins in place of RST/RSTSEL; DAC8555 is the external-reference version.
